title: Theseus: The Road of Trials
subtitle: Five bandits, one morning's walk, a hero's reputation

learningObjectives.text: Name the dangers Theseus cleared on the road to Athens
What was Theseus's signature method against each bandit?

plutarch.author: Plutarch

plutarch.excerpt: in a set combat, he slew Periphetes, in the neighborhood of Epidaurus, who used a club for his arms, and from thence had the name of Corynetes, or the club-bearer
plutarch.note: Verbatim passage; locator selects this local source segment.

narrativeBlocks.title: Periphetes the Club-Bearer
narrativeBlocks.body: Near Epidaurus, a bandit with an iron club stops travellers and beats them to death. Theseus challenges him, wins the fight, and takes the club — the first weapon he ever carries, and a trophy he keeps for life.

narrativeBlocks.title: Sinis the Pine-Bender
narrativeBlocks.body: At the Isthmus of Corinth, Sinis ties travellers to two bent pine trees and lets them spring upright. Theseus turns the trick on its inventor — Sinis dies by his own method.

narrativeBlocks.title: The Crommyonian Sow
narrativeBlocks.body: A monstrous wild sow called Phaea ravages the countryside near Crommyon. Theseus goes out of his way to hunt and kill her — the first deed that protects not travellers but whole villages.

narrativeBlocks.title: Sciron of the Cliff
narrativeBlocks.body: On the cliffs of Megara, Sciron forces passers-by to wash his feet — then kicks them into the sea, where a giant turtle waits below. Theseus hurls Sciron off the same rock.

narrativeBlocks.title: Procrustes' Bed
narrativeBlocks.body: The last stop before Athens: Procrustes offers travellers a bed for the night, then stretches the short and hammers down the tall to fit it exactly. Theseus puts him on his own bed. The road to Athens is finally safe — and 'the Procrustean bed' becomes a byword for forced conformity.

quiz.prompt: What pattern unites Theseus's victories on the road to Athens?

choices.text: He spares each bandit after winning their surrender
The gods strike each bandit before Theseus arrives
He turns each bandit's own cruelty back on them — club, pines, cliff, and bed
He traps each bandit in the labyrinth

quiz.explanation: Plutarch notes Theseus acted 'in imitation of Hercules, who always returned upon his assailants the same sort of' violence they dealt others.

quiz.prompt: Which bandit forced travellers to wash his feet before kicking them off a cliff?

choices.text: Sciron — Theseus hurled him off the same rock at Megara
